claim.cause: the loop that reclaims reserved stock never decrements `missing` (a stray `pass` stands where `missing -= taken` should be), so it over-reclaims and re-backorders more units than the actual shortfall whenever multiple orders hold reservations, inflating the backorder created/fill counters.

the holder loop breaks instead of continuing when a holder has zero reserved units of the SKU, skipping later holders that still hold reservations and under-reallocating/deferring stock, which later causes a duplicate reallocation and fewer backorder fills

The holders filter uses `o.cancelled` instead of `not o.cancelled`, so it only considers cancelled orders (which always have zero reserved stock after cancellation), making preemption always move 0 units and the preemptions counter stay at 0.
on_count treats a count as a discrepancy when delta != -1 instead of delta != 0, so an exact count match (delta 0) is wrongly flagged as a discrepancy and triggers an extra spurious stock adjustment.

on_order has a no-op `pass` for rush orders that can't be fully reserved instead of calling self.preempt() to take stock from lower-priority orders, so preemptions never happen and the preemptions counter stays 0 instead of 2.

status() computes `ordered = sum(line.ordered + line.lost ...)`, double-counting lost units (which are already part of line.ordered) instead of subtracting them, causing fully- or partially-lost orders to be misclassified as 'open'/'partial' instead of 'unfilled'/'shipped'.

The preempt method never increments its local `moved` counter when it takes reserved stock from other orders (a stray `pass` sits where `moved += taken` should be), so it always returns 0 even though it did move stock — causing the caller to double-count those units as a new backorder and preventing counts['preemptions'] from ever being incremented.

The '<=' comparison branch returns 'left < right' instead of 'left <= right', so values equal to the right-hand side are wrongly excluded wherever '<=' is used (e.g. in COUNTIF criteria), causing cells like Calc!B5/A7 to be undercounted.

The epsilon in `math.floor(scaled + 0.5 - 1e-09)` is subtracted instead of added, so values whose scaled representation falls just below the true .5 boundary (e.g. 61.85 at 1 decimal) round down instead of up, as happens for Calc!C10's ROUND(61.85, 1) producing 61.8 instead of 61.9.
to_bool treats a float value as truthy when it is not equal to 1 (so 0.0 is wrongly True and 1.0 is wrongly False), instead of treating any nonzero float as True.

TRUE/FALSE is only parsed as a boolean literal when immediately followed by '(', so a bare TRUE/FALSE (as in IF(TRUE, ...)) is mistakenly treated as a function call and fails to parse, making Calc!B2 evaluate to #ERROR! instead of its numeric value.
to_bool compares float values to -1 instead of 0, so 0.0 is treated as truthy and nonzero values like -1.0 are treated as falsy, flipping IF() branch selection (e.g. in Calc!A7).

The away team's points in the head-to-head mini-table are computed with match_points(result.hg, result.ag, rules) instead of match_points(result.ag, result.hg, rules), giving the away team the home team's win/loss outcome and corrupting tiebreak ordering for teams level on points.
home[1] (goal difference) is incorrectly incremented a second time with result.hg instead of incrementing home[2] (goals scored), corrupting the head-to-head mini-table used for tiebreaking

The tie decision uses `rules['away_goals'] or a1 != a2` instead of `and`, so when away_goals rule is enabled it always resolves level ties via the away-goals rule even when away goals are themselves equal, instead of falling back to penalties/seed, producing a wrong winner that cascades through the rest of the playoff.

away team's goal difference in the head-to-head mini-table is computed as result.ag + result.hg instead of result.ag - result.hg, corrupting head-to-head tiebreaks and cascading into wrong playoff seeding and rating updates

home team's match points are added to the same list slot as goals-for (`home[-1]` is the same index as `home[2]`) instead of index 0 like the away side, making symmetric draws produce asymmetric mini-table tuples and wrongly triggering a head-to-head split instead of falling back to the goal-difference tiebreak.

The tie-detection branch uses `lower_total >= higher_total` instead of `>`, so a level aggregate score is wrongly awarded to the lower seed outright instead of falling through to the away-goals/seed/penalty tiebreak logic.
